nodes.name: When Called
nodes.notes: ADR-061 Block 2 — services the TRIGGERING task's tail as client-side custom tools from Execute Agent Session's poll loop. IN: tool_name (get_task_comments|get_parent_chain|list_attachments|get_attachment), clickup_task_id (the TRIGGERING task id, set by n8n from the trigger — the scope pin; the agent CANNOT widen it), tool_input_json (the agent's raw tool input — only limit/since/depth/attachment_id are read from it, never a task id). OUT: { status, tool_result_content_json (a user.custom_tool_result content[] the agent SEES), new_warnings_json:'[]', new_images_json:'[]' }. All reads are on the BOT token (the caller @-mentioned the agent here -> has access; bot has access; byte-identical — per-user scoping earns its keep only for OTHER-task discovery, which stays on the clickup_* MCP). Branch-free terminal (Return re-reads Merge Result). The handler SELF-ALERTS a WARN on a side branch (Should Warn? -> Post Alert) on its own failure modes and returns new_warnings_json='[]' so the session does NOT double-fire; reused sub-workflows (Assemble Task Context) keep their own side-branch alerts.

nodes.name: Route Tool
nodes.notes: Route by tool_name to the right reused reader. 0 comments -> Assemble Task Context (v1); 1 parents -> Assemble Parent Context (v1); 2 attachments -> bot GET /task (native attachment index, NO extraction); 3 attachment -> Read Input (v1) single-attachment mode (only_att_id) + Upload Input Images (v1) for vision. Fallback (4 unknown) -> Build Unknown Result (defensive: Execute Agent Session only routes the 4 known names, so this is a routing-bug guard that still answers the agent + WARNs).

nodes.name: Call Assemble Task Context
nodes.notes: get_task_comments: reuse Assemble Task Context (v1) (eL3fJuRMpzVRuVUT) — the triggering task's comments + interleaved threaded replies on the bot token. It SELF-ALERTS on fetch/reply failure (its own side-branch Post Alert), so Build Comments Result only adds a WARN for a TOTAL sub-call failure (onError -> no task_comments key). onError=continueRegularOutput so a sub-call failure degrades to a structured tool result, never throws into the session.

nodes.name: Build Comments Result
nodes.notes: Shape Assemble Task Context's task_comments into a user.custom_tool_result text block. Optional tool args: limit (cap most-recent N) + since (ms-epoch floor). An empty thread is LEGITIMATE (no WARN). WARN only when the sub-call returned no task_comments key at all (total failure caught by onError). new_warnings_json='[]' (handler self-alerts on the side branch).

nodes.name: Call Assemble Parent Context
nodes.notes: get_parent_chain: reuse Assemble Parent Context (v1) (qgM37HdQj78Rn090) — depth-bounded ancestor titles/descriptions on the bot token. Its Fetch L0 throws on a bad id; onError=continueRegularOutput here catches it -> Build Parents Result detects no current_task and WARNs. A task with NO parent legitimately returns ancestor_chain=[] (no WARN).

nodes.name: Build Parents Result
nodes.notes: Shape Assemble Parent Context's ancestor_chain (general -> nearest) into a text block. Optional tool arg depth caps to the nearest N ancestors. No parent -> a clear 'no parents' answer (no WARN). WARN only when current_task is absent (the sub-call failed). new_warnings_json='[]' (self-alert).

nodes.name: Get Attachment List
nodes.notes: list_attachments: bot GET /api/v2/task/{id} for ClickUp's NATIVE attachment index (id/title/extension/mimetype/size) — NO bytes, NO Docling (cheap metadata-first, ADR-061 decision #3). Same endpoint Read Input's Get Task uses. onError=continueRegularOutput + retry so a transient ClickUp blip degrades to a structured 'list failed' tool result + WARN instead of throwing into the session.

nodes.name: Build Attachments Result
nodes.notes: Shape the task's attachments[] into a cheap index the agent reads to decide what to pull: one line per attachment with attachment_id, title, mime/ext, size. ADR-061 Block 2c: each ZIP attachment also nests its INNER manifest inline (indented), each inner file as attachment_id="<zip>:<idx>" with name/type/size (route=drop entries flagged [POMINIETO]); the agent pulls ONE inner file via get_attachment("<zip>:<idx>"). Manifests come from Fetch Zip Manifest (aligned by order with Build Zip Manifest Reqs[kind=zip]). No attachments -> legitimate empty (no WARN). WARN when the GET failed (no attachments array) OR a zip manifest failed (entries=null -> the zip is still listed plain, agent can pull the whole archive). new_warnings_json='[]' (self-alert via Should Warn?).

nodes.name: Build Read Input Args
nodes.notes: get_attachment: parse attachment_id from the agent's tool_input_json and emit { clickup_task_id, only_att_id } for Read Input single-attachment mode. _missing_id guards the Has Att Id? branch: an EMPTY only_att_id must NOT reach Read Input (empty = no filter = extract ALL attachments), so a missing id routes to Build Missing Id Result instead.

nodes.name: Has Att Id?
nodes.notes: TRUE: attachment_id present -> Read Input (single) extracts that ONE attachment. FALSE: no id -> Build Missing Id Result guides the agent to list_attachments first (and does NOT extract everything).

nodes.name: Call Read Input (single)
nodes.notes: get_attachment: Read Input (v1) (zgGpONulGMohQQqI) on the BOT token (no as_user_token) with only_att_id set -> its Explode Attachments filters to that ONE attachment (ADR-061 Block 0 single-attachment mode). Returns { blocks, clickup_task_id, warnings } for just that attachment (Docling text for docs; an image block for images). No match -> the no-attachment passthrough -> blocks=[] -> Build Attachment Result answers 'not found' + WARN. onError=continueRegularOutput so an extraction failure degrades, never throws.

nodes.name: Upload Tail Images
nodes.notes: If the pulled attachment is an IMAGE, upload it to the Files API via Upload Input Images (v1) (2VkZN5UeqVk6MDLW) so the agent SEES it as a vision block (file_id), mirroring the extract handler. input_images_json = Read Input's image-typed blocks. onError=continueRegularOutput so an upload failure degrades to a text marker per image (Build Attachment Result), never throws. For a document (no image blocks) Upload returns an empty file_map and this is a no-op.

value.input_images_json: ={{ JSON.stringify((((($('Call Read Input (single)').first()||{}).json||{}).blocks)||[]).filter(function(b){ return b && b.type === 'image' && ['image/png','image/jpeg','image/jpg','image/gif','image/webp'].indexOf(String(b.mime||'').toLowerCase()) >= 0; })) }}

nodes.name: Build Attachment Result
nodes.notes: Mirror of the extract handler's Build Extract Result (bot path, no as-U denial): blocks sorted by order -> text verbatim (incl. [BRAK..] markers) + image blocks resolved to {type:image,source:{type:file,file_id}} from the upload file_map (a failed upload -> a text marker). Empty (id not found / extraction empty) -> a clear 'not found, check list_attachments' result + WARN. [BRAK markers or failed images -> partial + WARN. new_warnings_json='[]' (self-alert); new_images_json='[]' (a pulled image is CONSUMED by the agent, not a produced output file).

nodes.name: Build Missing Id Result
nodes.notes: get_attachment called with no attachment_id: answer the agent with guidance (call list_attachments first) so the session resumes. This is the AGENT's input error, not a system failure -> NO WARN (avoid channel noise).

nodes.name: Build Unknown Result
nodes.notes: Defensive fallback: an unknown tool_name (Execute Agent Session only routes the 4 known names, so reaching here is a routing bug). Answer the agent 'not supported' so the session never stalls, and WARN (this should never fire in normal operation).

nodes.name: Merge Result
nodes.notes: Converge the five mutually-exclusive branches (0 comments, 1 parents, 2 attachments, 3 get_attachment-ok, 4 errors=missing-id+unknown) into ONE stream. Append; exactly one branch executes per call. Return re-reads this node so the contract is deterministic (branch-free terminal rule).

nodes.name: Should Warn?
nodes.notes: Side branch off the canonical result: TRUE when a Build node set _warn_source (a real handler failure mode: comments/parents/attachments/extraction failure, or unknown tool). TRUE -> Post Alert (one WARN). FALSE -> straight to Merge Tail. Both rejoin at Merge Tail -> Return; Return re-reads Merge Result so the alert side-trip can't corrupt the returned contract (mirrors Execute Agent Session).

nodes.name: Post Alert
nodes.notes: Centralized Post Alert (v1) seam (ADR-025, YSCdHlmdf3p9XEUx) — WARN, never post to ClickUp directly. Fires on the handler's own failure modes (the reused Assemble Task Context fires its OWN comment/reply alerts separately). onError=continueRegularOutput so an alert-channel hiccup never breaks the handler return. No loop risk: trigger is executeWorkflow (the session), not a webhook watching the Alerts task.

nodes.name: Merge Tail
nodes.notes: Rejoin the alerted (input 0) and not-alerted (input 1) paths into the single terminal input. Append; exactly one executes.

nodes.name: Return
nodes.notes: SOLE TERMINAL. Re-reads Merge Result's first item (the canonical result, NOT Merge Tail's direct input which Post Alert would have replaced — research-the-web return-determinism idiom) and returns the clean handler contract { status, tool_result_content_json, new_images_json, new_warnings_json } that Execute Agent Session's Build Tail Result Text consumes. Internal _warn_* fields are dropped here.

nodes.name: Build Zip Manifest Reqs
nodes.notes: ADR-061 Block 2c: emit one item per ZIP attachment of the triggering task ({kind:'zip', zip_att_id, url, title, task_id}) so Fetch Zip Manifest can pull each archive's INNER manifest (cheap, no extraction). No zips -> a single {kind:'none'} sentinel so the chain still reaches Build Attachments Result (a 0-item Code node would skip everything downstream). Reads the same attachment index Get Attachment List fetched.

nodes.name: Is Zip Req?
nodes.notes: TRUE (kind=zip) -> Fetch Zip Manifest pulls that archive's inner manifest. FALSE (the kind='none' sentinel, no zips) -> straight to Merge Manifests so Build Attachments Result still runs. Exactly one branch fires per item; with >=1 zip only TRUE fires (N items), with 0 zips only FALSE fires (1 sentinel).

nodes.name: Fetch Zip Manifest

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ url: $json.url, task_id: $json.task_id, attachment_id: $json.zip_att_id, parent_title: $json.title, manifest_only: true, caps: $json.caps }) }}

nodes.notes: ADR-061 Block 2c: POST the zip's pre-signed ClickUp url to the zip-extractor in MANIFEST mode (manifest_only:true) -> central-directory walk only: names/sizes/types/routes + <zip>:<idx> att_ids, NO byte read / upload / sign. Runs once per zip item. Caps omitted -> service defaults (50/25/250) which equal config; entry indices are cap-independent so they still align with get_attachment's single-entry materialize. onError continueRegularOutput + retry: a manifest failure degrades to no entries (Build Attachments Result lists the zip plain + WARNs), never throws.

nodes.name: Merge Manifests
nodes.notes: ADR-061 Block 2c: rejoin the zip branch (input 0, Fetch Zip Manifest) and the no-zip branch (input 1, Is Zip Req? false) into ONE input for Build Attachments Result (a Code node with two incoming connections would run once per connection). Append; exactly one input fires per run (mirrors Merge Result).

nodes.name: Lookup Zip Caps (Tail)

parameters.query:
select
  max(value::int) filter (where key = 'zip_max_entries')               as zip_max_entries,
  max(value::int) filter (where key = 'zip_max_file_mb')               as zip_max_file_mb,
  max(value::int) filter (where key = 'zip_max_total_uncompressed_mb') as zip_max_total_uncompressed_mb
from config;

nodes.notes: ADR-061 Block 2c follow-on: read the LIVE zip caps from config so list_attachments' manifest-mode extractor call uses the SAME caps as get_attachment's single-entry materialize (Read Input's Zip Caps). Chained LINEARLY before Build Zip Manifest Reqs so it always executes first (avoids the unexecuted-node race that bit Read Input's parallel Lookup). onError continueRegularOutput + alwaysOutputData so a DB blip degrades to defaults 50/25/250 (Build Zip Manifest Reqs falls back) instead of failing list_attachments.

nodes.name: Get Task Details
nodes.notes: get_task_details: bot GET /api/v2/task/{id} for the TRIGGERING task's own title + description + status (ADR-061 Block 2c follow-on — the managed floor no longer loads the description eagerly; the agent pulls it here when the request needs the task spec). Same endpoint as Get Attachment List. onError continueRegularOutput + retry so a ClickUp blip degrades to a 'details failed' result + WARN instead of throwing into the session.

nodes.name: Build Details Result
nodes.notes: Shape the triggering task's title + description (markdown_description preferred) + status into a user.custom_tool_result text block. The managed floor lists only the title and a 'call get_task_details for the spec' hint, so this is where the agent actually reads the description. WARN only when the GET failed (no task object). new_warnings_json='[]' (self-alert via Should Warn?).
